pricing.rule: Each delivered call bills price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005. A call runs only when its full delivered amount fits the batch's remaining max_usd, so max_usd must be at least Σ(price_usd × 1.15 + $0.005).

STAMP proved Zcash can carry a record of a burn. you destroy a token, you get a receipt.

we built what it could have been: you burn, you get paid, and then you get the receipt/stamp on Zcash mainnet.

every coin planted on Sapling is a pump.fun coin, paired with ZEC instead of SOL. same curve, same graduation, same terminals. one difference: every coin has roots.

comment.comment:
Sapling ($SAPLING) is the first and only fully Zcash-native launchpad & terminal — a ~$2–3M market-cap product generating real, on-chain revenue at a pace that makes it look severely undervalued.

In roughly 36 days since launch (late September 2026), the protocol has processed ~$40–42M in trading volume, launched 430+ coins (28 graduated into their own ZEC pools), paid ~140+ ZEC (~$175–180K) directly to holders, burned ~220M $SAPLING (~22% of supply via the 0.5% buy-and-burn), and added substantial ZEC to the $SAPLING/ZEC liquidity pool. Cumulative protocol revenue has already crossed $500K, with ~90% flowing back out (holders in ZEC, burns, and liquidity). DefiLlama shows trailing 30-day fees of ~$464K and revenue of ~$279K — an annualized run-rate of roughly $4.8M in fees and $2.9M in revenue against a sub-$3M fully diluted valuation.

The use case is unmatched in its niche. Coins launch and trade paired against ZEC (not SOL), every trade feeds a per-coin “roots” ZEC vault that holders can harvest by burning their tokens in the same transaction, and users can launch, trade, and cash out straight from a Zcash wallet (including shielded paths via integrations like Noir/Zodl and Near Intents). No Phantom, no SOL required for core flows, with receipts (“stamps”) on Zcash mainnet and full on-chain transparency of every fee split, burn, and payout. It is the bridge that lets Solana’s memecoin volume touch Zcash’s privacy without forcing traders to abandon one for the other. Nothing else does this combination of ZEC pairing, roots/harvest mechanics, Zcash-wallet-native terminal, and real ZEC yield.

The team has shipped religiously. The public changelog and X updates show continuous delivery: launch + roots/harvest/stamps + security-reviewed vault on day one, rapid graduation of $SAPLING itself, Terminal, multi-quote (ZEC/hSOL/stocks), Robinhood Chain (Pons) integration, developer API/SDK, ZSA testnet twins (open source), liquidity and foundation donations, site rebuilds, and dozens of incremental improvements — 70+ updates in the first month with everything verifiable on-chain. Dev supply was locked early and treasury buybacks are burned. This is not a vapor roadmap; it is a product that has been live and iterating in public from the start.

What’s still to come amplifies the asymmetry: fuller Terminal coverage across Robinhood Chain launchpads, a browser-extension Sapling wallet, collectibles living on Zcash, native ZSAs (so Sapling coins become first-class shielded Zcash assets the day they hit mainnet), and shielded holder rewards post-NU7. At current valuations the market is pricing a one-month-old niche launchpad, not a revenue-generating privacy bridge with proven shipping velocity and clear catalysts into deeper Zcash integration.

I know where im placing my conviction. Do you?

comment.comment:
Crypto Investors Horrified After Memecoin Launchpad Introduces Concept Of Financial Consequences

SOLANA — Panic spread across cryptocurrency markets after developers unveiled Sapling ($SAPLING), a Zcash-powered memecoin launchpad that allows traders to create speculative assets while accumulating actual reserves.

“This is an existential threat to our industry,” explained one investor. “For years, we’ve perfected the art of launching thousands of coins backed by absolutely nothing. Now these lunatics want collateral?”

Sapling allows newly launched tokens to accumulate ZEC reserves from trading fees, creating a system where holders can burn their tokens to redeem a proportional share of accumulated assets.

Analysts described the development as particularly concerning because it introduces an unfamiliar concept to cryptocurrency markets: something potentially remaining after everyone stops believing in it.

Even worse, trading fees can fund SAPLING buybacks and burns, directly linking launchpad activity to token scarcity.

“First they introduce reserves, then redemptions, and next they’ll expect us to understand balance sheets,” warned one trader.

Industry experts fear Sapling could become a serious competitor to Pump.fun by combining speculative token launches with Zcash-backed economics.

Developers have reportedly been urged to immediately discontinue the redemption mechanism and replace it with an AI agent that tweets inspirational quotes.

At press time, investors were demanding that Sapling abandon its financial infrastructure and launch a frog-themed token instead.
